audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3 and Level 6 were scored 'Skill' and 2+ items was given to Darius.
audit.why: The mirror (darius__ryze) already corrected this chart so every stage before 2+ items reads Darius, with 2+ items flipped to Ryze — the two directions have to agree. It is also what the packet says, and what this page's own whys[6] and late block argue: two-item Ryze out-damages him in extended fights, everything before that belongs to Darius.
audit.corrected: Rows 2, 4 and 6 flipped in both layers as matched pairs with ratings moved to 3/10, 3/10 and 6/10, and the two pieces of text that argued the wrong side (whys[4], spikes[1]) rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page keys itself to Apprehend without ever giving its cooldown, and spikes[1] calls Level 3 Ryze's "first real threat window" while the chart hands that stage to Darius.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 from 535 range, falling to 16s at rank 5 — that is the longest gap in his kit and the only honest step-up window in the lane. Decimate meanwhile drops from 9s to 5s and heals him off every champion the blade catches, which is why the level 3 trade does not belong to Ryze.
audit.corrected: Apprehend's 26s/535 written into the spike and the do; Decimate's rank-3 7s cooldown and blade heal given as the reason level 3 is his.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] and early say Ryze must reach melee range to apply Flux. mid describes "his Q passive (empowered Crippling Strike spin that heals on the outer ring)", which merges two different abilities. spikes[0] asserts Apprehend is online at level 1. Crippling Strike's auto-reset is never named as the burst tell.
audit.why: Spell Flux is 615 and Overload is 1000 — neither is melee, and 615 is comfortably outside Apprehend's 535 hook, which is the actual spacing rule. Decimate (Q) is the wide axe swing whose blade hits harder and heals him; Crippling Strike (W) is a separate 5s auto-reset that slows. Nobody has two abilities at level 1, so which one he takes is a read, not a fact. And the reset wind-up, not the ability cast, is the tell that the all-in has started.
audit.corrected: Real ranges given as the spacing rule (615 versus his 535), Decimate and Crippling Strike separated and described correctly, the level-1 assertion softened to 'once Apprehend is up', and the auto-reset added as the burst tell.

edits.before: Realm Warp opens flanks and escapes, and your EQ DPS now duels most tops on their cooldown gaps.
edits.after: Noxian Guillotine executes off five Hemorrhage stacks — Realm Warp answers the map, not him.

edits.before: Darius whiffs Apprehend (Pull) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Apprehend whiffs and you own 26 seconds — that is the whole window.

edits.before: That is Darius’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Crippling Strike is an auto reset — that wind-up means the hook already landed.

edits.before: You have only Q and must approach melee range to activate Flux — Darius punishes with auto-E-auto Hemorrhage stacking before any trade pattern exists for you.
edits.after: Overload reaches 1000, but Spell Flux needs 615 and Apprehend hooks from 535 — every step inside that gives him Hemorrhage stacks before you have a trade pattern.

edits.before: Your E-W-Q combo through Fluxed minions is live, but Darius's level 3 empowered Q spin heals the chip and threatens a five-stack all-in if you misjudge distance.
edits.after: Your Flux-then-root chain is live, but Decimate's blade heals him off every champion it catches and a five-stack Hemorrhage all-in punishes one misjudged step.

edits.before: Realm Warp adds map pressure and flank angles, and your EQ DPS is now a real threat — neither side cleanly owns a straight 1v1 at this stage.
edits.after: Realm Warp adds map pressure and flank angles but no combat steroid — Noxian Guillotine is true damage that scales with Hemorrhage, so the 1v1 is still his.

edits.before: Darius's E (Apprehend) comes online at level 1 and every Hemorrhage stack he lands before your combo is ready punishes your melee-range Flux pattern before it starts.
edits.after: Once Apprehend is up it hooks from 535 on a 26-second rank-1 cooldown, and every Hemorrhage stack he lands before your chain exists punishes the walk to 615.

edits.before: Your full combo loop (E-Flux into W root into empowered Q) lets you trade through Fluxed minions and walk away with Phase Rush — your first real threat window.
edits.after: Decimate is down to 7s at rank 3 and its blade heals him off you — your Flux-root-Overload trade only breaks even if you leave before Hemorrhage climbs.

edits.before: Level 1 is simply survive: you have only Q, and Darius walks at you with E up and passive Hemorrhage ready to stack on any auto he lands. Hug the back of the wave, last-hit with Q at maximum range, and do not give him a free Apprehend target — the pull is the starting gun for every Darius kill. At level 2 your W root is online but spending it as an opener into Apprehend's range is suicide; save it as an escape tool so a misplayed trade doesn't become a death. Level 3 is your first real breath: E a minion adjacent to him, W root through the wave so minions absorb the Flux bounce, double-Q as Phase Rush fires, and use the speed boost to exit his answer range before Hemorrhage reaches five stacks.
edits.after: Level 1 is simply survive: you have only Overload, and Hemorrhage stacks off every auto he lands. Hug the back of the wave, last-hit from the end of Q's 1000 range, and never stand inside 535 where Apprehend hooks — the pull is the starting gun for every Darius kill. At level 2 your root is online but only against a Fluxed target, and Spell Flux costs you the walk to 615; spending it as an opener inside his hook range is a death, so hold it to escape. Level 3 is a breath, not a window: Flux the minion beside him, root through the wave, Overload twice as Phase Rush fires, and leave on the speed before Hemorrhage reaches five.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are a grind you manage, not a window you force — his Q passive (empowered Crippling Strike spin that heals on the outer ring) and Hemorrhage make sustained fights punishing if you are already chipped. Farm with E-Q from max range, use the wave's Flux bounce to avoid walking into Apprehend's cone, and bank Manaflow stacks toward your item timing. Level 6 adds Realm Warp: you gain genuine macro pressure and can threaten flank angles your jungler can build on, but you get no combat steroid, so do not confuse map utility with a 1v1 power spike — Darius still wins a straight slugfest here. Use Warp to set up 2v2s where your W root is worth two lockups, not one.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are a grind you manage, not a window you force — Decimate's blade heals him off anyone it catches and Crippling Strike is a 5-second auto reset that slows, so a chipped Ryze loses every long exchange. Farm from max Overload range, bounce Flux off the wave instead of walking to 535, and bank Manaflow toward your item timing. Level 6 adds Realm Warp: real macro pressure and flank angles for your jungler, but no combat steroid, so do not mistake map utility for a duel spike — Noxian Guillotine is true damage and Darius still wins the slugfest. Use Warp to make 2v2s where your root counts twice.

notes: Chart aligned to the mirror's correction (Darius owns every stage through First item, Ryze takes 2+ items). Two mechanical errors fixed beyond the names: the page said Ryze must reach melee range to apply Flux — Spell Flux is 615, which is the entire spacing story against a 535 hook — and mid merged Decimate and Crippling Strike into one 'Q passive empowered Crippling Strike spin'. They are separate abilities: Decimate is the wide swing that heals off blade hits, Crippling Strike is a 5s auto-reset slow. Confirming the mirror's systemic note from this side: the root is Rune Prison (W) and it only roots if Spell Flux (E) is already on the target, otherwise it is a slow — that gate is what makes or breaks every anti-Apprehend play here.
